title: Population pyramids & DTM
examples: How do I read the different sections of a population pyramid?
What does a high dependency ratio mean for a country?
Can you show me an example of a country at Stage 2?

explain.say: Today we learn about population pyramids and the demographic transition model. This model shows how populations change over time. We will learn about the different stages of this change.

items: Stage 2: Early Expanding (High birth, falling death)
Stage 3: Late Expanding (Falling birth, low death)
Stage 4: Low Stationary (Low birth, low death)
Stage 5: Declining (Very low birth, low death)

explain.say: Stage two is when death rates start to fall quickly. This happens because of better health and medicine. Birth rates remain high for a while. This causes a rapid population increase.
Stage three shows that birth rates begin to fall. People start to have fewer children for various reasons. The population continues to grow, but the rate of growth slows down. This is a key change.
The dependency ratio measures the number of people not working. This includes young people and older people. It compares them to the working-age population. A high ratio means more dependents.

A real-life example is Japan. It is often seen as being in Stage 5. This means very low birth rates and low death rates. The pyramid shape is very narrow at the base. This shows a shrinking population.

A common mistake is thinking that a wide base always means a growing population. A wide base means high birth rates, but if death rates are also very high, growth can still be slow. Always look at the death rate too.

items: High birth rate is one factor.
Low death rate is another factor.

draw.text: Base width does not equal growth

faq.q: What does a very wide base on a pyramid mean?
faq.a: It means a very high number of births are happening in that population. This suggests a high birth rate is present. You might also ask: What does a wide base indicate? Or, what does a pyramid with a wide bottom show?
asks: What does a wide base mean?
What does a high birth rate show on a pyramid?

faq.q: How do I know which stage a country is in?
faq.a: You must look at both the birth rate and the death rate together. For example, Stage 2 has high births and falling deaths. You could also ask: What combination of rates shows Stage 3? Or, how do I identify the stage?
asks: How do I classify the stage?

faq.q: What exactly is the dependency ratio?
faq.a: It is a ratio that compares non-working people to working-age people. This helps us understand the strain on resources. You might also ask: What does the dependency ratio measure? Or, what is the ratio of dependents?
asks: What is the dependency ratio for?

faq.q: Does a low dependency ratio mean a country is doing well?
faq.a: It suggests that the working population is large compared to dependents. However, this can also mean the population is aging. You could ask: Is a low dependency ratio always good? Or, what does a low ratio imply?
asks: Is a low dependency ratio always positive?
What does a low ratio suggest?

faq.q: What does Stage 5 look like on a pyramid?
faq.a: It looks like a top-heavy pyramid, with the base being very narrow. This shows fewer babies being born than in previous stages. You could also ask: What is the shape of a declining population? Or, what does Stage 5 show?
asks: What is the shape for Stage 5?

facts: Stage 1 has both high birth rates and high death rates.
The demographic transition model describes changes in birth and death rates.
A high dependency ratio means fewer working people for dependents.
Stage 2 is characterized by falling death rates.

quiz.say: A population pyramid with a very wide base and a narrow top is most likely in which stage?
quiz.why: Stage 2 has high birth rates and falling death rates, leading to a wide base.

wrong.1: Stage 1 has high death rates which would narrow the pyramid more than shown.
wrong.2: Stage 3 shows falling birth rates, which would make the base narrower than shown.
wrong.3: Stage 4 has low birth rates, so the base would not be as wide.

quiz.say: Which indicator is calculated by comparing the number of young and old people to the working-age group?
quiz.why: The dependency ratio specifically compares non-working age groups to the working-age group.

wrong.0: The birth rate only measures the number of live births over a period.
wrong.1: The death rate only measures the number of deaths over a period.
wrong.2: Population size is the total number of people, not a ratio comparison.
